task.description: Start a sub-agent with a fresh context and get back only its final report. agent "explore" is read-only and fast: use it for broad research ("where is X handled", "how does Y work"). agent "general" may also edit files and run commands: use it for a self-contained job. Several task calls in one turn run in parallel. The sub-agent does not see this conversation, so the prompt must contain everything it needs: the goal, where to look, and what the report must contain.

description.description: Three to six words naming the job.

prompt.description: The complete task and what the report should contain.

agent.description: explore (default): read and search only. general: may also edit and run commands, with the usual permission questions.

create_agent.description: Create a reusable sub-agent as a file that the task tool can start by name afterwards (like a custom agent in Claude Code). Use it when a kind of job comes back again and again (review, test writing, migrations, research in one area). The user is asked before it is written. Give it a short lowercase name, a description of when to use it, the tools it may use (for example read_file, grep, glob, list_dir for a reviewer that must not change anything; leave the list empty for all tools) and its instructions: what it does, how it works and what its report looks like.

name.description: Lowercase letters, digits, - and _ (for example code-reviewer).

description.description: One sentence: when to use this agent.

instructions.description: The system prompt of the agent.

tools.description: Tool names it may use; empty means all.
